summary.verdict: This is a real business plan, not a sketch: the six-year roadmap, the regulatory comparison, the nine risks with mitigations and the stakeholder grid already answer more of the ballot than two of the seven winning pages did. What holds it back is not missing work but disagreement inside the work. Prices, dates, markets, SDG numbers, the third protein and the kill switch each appear in two or three different versions across this page and the Laws, Human Practices, Sustainability and Geospatial pages, and a judge who notices one stops trusting the rest.
strengths: The regulatory comparison in section 7: two routes, their cost in time, the choice, and what is deferred.
The roadmap in section 6.1 is text, with durations and done counts, so a judge can audit it. Several winners buried theirs in images.
Honest sentences about your own product: it will not beat the best chemicals, the B. subtilis survival rate may be too low, Ms. Chen's objection that plants may stop building their own resilience.
Stakeholder entries that say what changed, especially dropping price competition with chemical fertilizers after Professor Chen's advice.
Risk mitigations written as tasks someone performs on a schedule, like the monthly membrane check with extension officers.
priorities: Fix the price. Pick one number and one currency, and make section 2.1, the Our solution box, section 6.2 and the Geospatial page's NT$30,000 agree.
Fix the contradictions with other ReLeaf pages: the contained-use pathway against Laws and Regulations, the kill switch against Human Practices, the SDG numbers against Sustainability.
Decide who buys first. Conventional smallholders in section 5.4 and organic farms in the obtainable market cannot both be the beachhead, and no first customer is named anywhere.
Add the two missing ballot answers: your team's own skills and gaps, and the negative long-term impacts of the finished product.
Make one decision per claim and delete the repeats: the mission appears three times, the PESTEL paragraphs restate the chart, and the value proposition sentence is used twice.

ballot.question: Has the team identified their first potential customers and their unmet need(s) that are not yet covered by existing solutions?
ballot.note: Eight stakeholder groups and six consultations are documented, but no first customer is named, nobody is quoted saying what they would buy, and the unmet need is never written as a list of conditions the product must meet.

ballot.question: Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?
ballot.where: 3. Business model (SWOT), 4. Market analysis (Strategic positioning, Competitor analysis), 6.1 Product development plan
ballot.note: Scale-up is planned unit by unit and the MVP figure appears twice, but MVP is never defined, the first-on-the-market claim carries no hedge or search, and the competitor table has slipped out of alignment.

ballot.question: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?
ballot.where: 6.1 Product development plan, 5.6 Marketing timeline, 6.2 Financial projection, 8. Potential risks
ballot.note: The strongest part of the page. Weakened by the 2026 against 2027 pilot dates, three different expansion orders, and the fixed cost that changes between the table and the break-even sum.

ballot.question: Has the team outlined the skills, capabilities, and the stakeholders required to be credible in developing their solution further?
ballot.where: 4. Market analysis (Key stakeholders), 3. Business model (Key partners, Key resources)
ballot.note: Stakeholders are well documented. The team's own skills, gaps and who would fill them are not mentioned anywhere, which is the cheapest missing section on the page.

ballot.question: Has the team considered the positive and negative long-term impacts of their fully developed solution?
ballot.where: 3. Business model (SWOT weaknesses and threats), 8. Potential risks, 9. Conclusion
ballot.note: Negatives exist as present-day risks, but the long-term view in the conclusion is all positive. No negative impact of the finished product is paired with a cause and a mitigation.

winners: Unmet need named as a gap in one sentence
Customers, from a class down to a named first customer
Solution and why it is inventive, against named competitors
Market size, TAM to SAM to SOM with the arithmetic shown
Money: costs, revenue model, funding plan
Risks as phase, risk and response
Downloads: business plan, pitch deck, financials
skeleton.gap: Five of the seven winners build their headings out of the five ballot questions, so a judge reaches each answer in one scroll. ReLeaf uses a consulting structure instead, which is what the two weakest winning pages did, and it hides three answers: the first customer sits inside Market analysis, the skills answer is missing, and the long-term negatives are scattered through SWOT and the risk table. Your order is also inside out at the start, with the product in section 1 and the problem folded away.

extras: Spelling: change “miniscule” to “minuscule” (section 1, climate box).
“Maintenance of the bioreactor is considerably minimal” does not make sense. Change it to “The bioreactor needs very little maintenance” (section 2.2).
“bioreactor repairment” is not a word. Change it to “bioreactor repairs” (section 2.2, The App).
Change “distinct from an Non-Governmental Organization (NGO)” to “different from a non-governmental organization (NGO)” (section 3.1).
“safety measures that reduce safety and regulatory concerns” says you reduce safety. Change it to “safety measures that reduce biosafety risks and regulatory concerns” (SWOT, Strengths).

The PESTEL intro stops at “legal lens we can see that” and never finishes. Change it to “Fig. 4 looks at our project through six lenses: political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal.”

The same sentence appears twice: “Overall, our system gives farmers an automatic, customizable, more effective, and sustainable way...” at the end of the canvas, and “Our system offers farmers an automatic, customizable, more effective, and sustainable way...” under Value proposition. Delete the first one.
Change “It also takes into great consideration of biosafety” to “It is also designed for biosafety” (Our solution box).
Tense: change “only 3.47% of Taiwan’s total farmland is organic and eco-friendly by 2024” to “only 3.47% of Taiwan’s farmland was organic or eco-friendly in 2024”.
Change “which earning their adoption would serve as an additional point of validation” to “and earning their trust would add credibility to our project” (Sustainable farming farmers).
Change “a Taiwan commercial indoor vertical farm” to “a Taiwanese commercial indoor vertical farm” (Yes Health iFarm).
Change “which they hold practical knowledge of purchasing behavior” to “so they know about purchasing behavior” (Agriculture distributor).
Two sentences joined by a comma. Change “agricultural standards, a single policy shift can make or break” to “agricultural standards. A single policy change can make or break” (Government).
Change “keep track with them” to “keep track of them” (World Vegetable Center).
One company, two spellings: “Agritalk” in the stakeholder grid and “AgriTalk” in the competitor summary. Check the company’s own spelling and use it in both places.
“collabs” is slang. Change “potential collabs” to “possible collaborations” (Key companies box).
Grammar: change “the interest in bioprotectants have also increased” to “interest in bioprotectants has also increased” (Market opportunities box).

“unlike current solutions which require farmers to constantly have to interpret” never finishes its comparison. Make it its own sentence: “Current solutions make farmers decide when, how much and where to apply protectants, which risks overuse or underuse.”
“leasing middlemen” means renting people. Change it to “working through distributors who sell our product to farmers” (section 5.3).
Fig. 9 is described as a “Barriers to entry table”, but there is no table or image, only four text blocks. Either add the table or delete the caption.
Grammar: change “can supports” to “can support” (section 5.6).
Change “allowing others to gain accessibility on our product” to “so that academic labs can buy and use our product” (Sales and Partnerships).
The roadmap caption “ReLeaf Strategic Master Roadmap. Unified 6-year Gantt chart.” has no figure number, between Fig. 10 and Fig. 11. Number it and renumber the figures after it.
The roadmap marks Year 1 “8/8 done”, but the Year 1 text says “the team will demonstrate”. If it is done, write “demonstrated”; if not, mark the rows as planned.
Change “pilot success metrics would be done with deploying about 20 to 50 prototype devices” to “in the field pilot we will deploy 20 to 50 prototype devices” (Year 2).

Phase numbers do not match. The Year 3 text says “phase 3 marks the transition from local to industrial scale”, but the roadmap labels scale-up “2Industrial scale-up” (and the Taiwan phase “1.2”). Use the same numbers in the text and the chart.
Change “Philippine is a promising market” to “The Philippines is a promising market” (Year 3).
Tense: change “is intensively managed and relied heavily” to “is intensively managed and relies heavily” (Year 3, Vietnam).
Year 4 says “The final phase focuses on deploying 500 to 1500 units”, but the roadmap has another phase after it (Global market expansion). Change “The final phase” to “This phase”.
Packaging has prices ($0.5 and $0.25 per unit) but is marked “N/A” and left out of the “Total variable cost $201.55”. Add it ($202.30) or say why packaging is not counted.
Two sentences joined by a comma. Change “not just for the Jamboree, we want to develop” to “not just for the Jamboree. We want to develop” (Stage 2).
Change “a evidence of crop benefit” to “evidence of crop benefit” (Stage 2).
The letters in “Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency (BAPHIQ)” do not match the name. Write the agency’s official English name in full and check that the acronym matches it (section 7).

notes.anchor: ReLeaf is an optogenetic bioreactor system that enables automated, on-demand protection
notes.title: Start with the farmer's problem
notes.body: The page opens with your machine. Your best numbers about crop loss sit in the folded box below, so a judge who does not open the fold never sees why this matters. Move one sourced sentence up here, then say what ReLeaf is.
notes.after: Heat and salt already cause about half of the world's crop losses each year (Bray et al., 2000). ReLeaf is a bioreactor that makes crop protectants on the farm, only when sensors show stress.
notes.excerpt_note: Leiden gives the number, the harm and the gap in four sentences before naming its own product.
notes.ballot: Has the team identified their first potential customers and their unmet need(s) that are not yet covered by existing solutions?

notes.anchor: automatically produces and releases protective proteins directly to the crop root zone
notes.title: Root zone or spraying, pick one
notes.body: Here the protectant goes into the root zone through irrigation. In section 2.2 it is “a cell-free liquid that the farmer can then use to spray on their crops”, and Fig. 2 step 3 says “spray in fields”. A judge will see two different products. Decide which one you built and use it everywhere.

notes.anchor: LEA 14 (abiotic stress protection), ACCD (ethylene reduction), and NaD1 (antifungal defense)
notes.title: Third protein has two names
notes.body: The antifungal protein is NaD1 here and in Stage 1 of the funding plan, but BoPep4 in the Year 1 roadmap and in the summary at the end of section 6.1. The Laws and Regulations page uses only BoPep4. Pick one name for this page and say in one clause how it relates to the other, if they are related.
notes.excerpt_note: A prize-winning page let one organism carry several names in one block. It is the first thing a careful reader notices.

notes.anchor: Mission statement: ReLeaf strengthens agricultural resilience by enabling automated, on-demand protection
notes.title: Mission repeats the first paragraph
notes.body: This sentence says the same thing as the first two sentences of the Overview, in almost the same words. Keep one of them.
notes.after: Delete this line and keep the Overview paragraph, which already states the mission.

notes.anchor: Vision: Every farmer is a biomanufacturer.
notes.title: Five words a judge will remember
notes.body: This is the strongest line on the page. It states your ambition in five plain words, and the sentence after it explains what that means in practice. Keep it exactly as it is.

notes.anchor: humanity is forced to choose between immediate technological adaptation or multi-system crop failure
notes.title: Drop the dramatic opener
notes.body: The sentences after this one carry real numbers with sources, and they are much stronger. This opening clause makes the reader wait for them.
notes.after: In a changing climate, seasons shift, temperatures swing, soil salinity rises and fungal outbreaks grow worse.

notes.anchor: compounding cellular damage in ways that can’t be triggered by either stress independently
notes.title: Say caused, not triggered
notes.body: As written this says the damage cannot be triggered, which is the opposite of your point. One word changes the meaning.
notes.after: compounding cellular damage in ways that neither stress causes on its own

notes.anchor: The price is about 100,000 to 150,000 in total for initial installation
notes.title: Four different prices, no currency
notes.body: The number above this line is 135,297.77 with no currency. This sentence says 100,000 to 150,000, also with no currency. In the Our solution box you write “$60,000 NTD”, and the Geospatial Analysis page builds its whole cost model on “unit cost (NT$30,000)”. Agree on one price and one currency with the Geospatial team, then write it the same way in all four places.
notes.after: One ReLeaf unit costs about NT$[number] to install. Prices vary with tiered pricing and subsidies.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: The system has three core components that work together to monitor field conditions
notes.title: Good signpost before three parts
notes.body: This sentence tells the reader what is coming, and the next three paragraphs deliver the Sensors, the Bioreactor and the App in that order. A judge can follow the product without a diagram.

notes.anchor: Consult with someone from our team/company to see the soil quality and condition of your farm
notes.title: Shorten the first setup step
notes.body: Step 1 is one 40-word sentence with “to see” twice. Shorter steps are easier for a farmer, and for a judge reading quickly.
notes.after: Ask our team to survey your farm. We check how many soil types you have and whether conditions change from one area to another.

notes.anchor: If you add the our line channel, you will be able to send messages/requests
notes.title: Fix the typo and explain LINE
notes.body: “add the our line channel” has an extra word. An international judge also will not know that LINE is the messaging app almost everyone in Taiwan uses, or what the Chinese account name means.
notes.after: You can also add our LINE account (LINE is the main messaging app in Taiwan) and send us questions or requests. Account name: 農友助手 (Farmer's Helper).

notes.anchor: What they do is instead of making farmers have to go through middlemen in order to sell their product
notes.title: Split this spoken sentence
notes.body: This sentence runs for about 60 words and holds three ideas, so the reader loses the thread. Say one thing per sentence.
notes.after: USE-GH buys crops from farmers directly, at a much lower fee than middlemen charge. It also teaches farmers to process their raw materials into finished products, so they earn more from the same harvest.

notes.anchor: Imperfections in the bioreactor could lead to dilution of the protectants, while biofouling inside the chambers may reduce protein yield
notes.title: Weaknesses name real mechanisms
notes.body: You name how the product could fail, not just that it might: dilution, biofouling, a blocked valve. That is far more convincing than a careful sentence about risk, and it tells a judge you understand your own hardware.
notes.excerpt_note: SUSTech-BIO writes each weakness as a process that goes wrong, in one line each.

notes.anchor: The global push to meet UN Sustainability Goals (particularly SDGs 2, 8, 11, 12, 13, and 15)
notes.title: SDG numbers clash with Sustainability
notes.body: This page claims SDGs 2, 8, 11, 12, 13 and 15, and the SDG box lower down repeats them. The Sustainability page chooses SDG 2, 4, 10 and 15, and says plainly that Climate Action “isn’t the main point of our project”. Two pages cannot pick different goals. Use the Sustainability page's four and link to it.

notes.anchor: Legal and regulatory frameworks also require a lot of careful navigation
notes.title: Six PESTEL paragraphs, one job
notes.body: All six paragraphs open the same way and mostly restate the chart above them. Keep the two that change a decision (the GMO rules and the subsidy route) and delete the rest. The page is long, and this is the cheapest place to shorten it.
notes.excerpt_note: A winner shipped two marketing sections that opened with the same paragraph. Read your opening sentences in a column and delete the repeats.

notes.anchor: Operating under a social enterprise model, we maintain an accessible, small basic fee structure
notes.title: The business has no name here
notes.body: The canvas figure calls the company GEMS Taiwan, but the text only ever says ReLeaf. A judge cannot tell whether ReLeaf is the product, the team or the company. Say it once, early in section 3.
notes.after: GEMS Taiwan is the social enterprise we would register; ReLeaf is the product it sells.

notes.anchor: By utilizing our optimized CcaS-CcaR two-component optogenetic system linked to automated LED arrays
notes.title: Gloss the light system once
notes.body: A business reader meets CcaS-CcaR here with no explanation. One short clause is enough, and the rest of the paragraph already says what it does.
notes.after: Green and red LEDs switch protein production on and off through our light-sensing system (CcaS-CcaR).

notes.anchor: A traditional business model canvas focuses on single value exchange
notes.title: This paragraph belongs one section up
notes.body: This explains the social business model canvas, which you presented in section 3. Sitting under Market analysis, it reads as if the canvas is about to start again. Move it to the top of the canvas section in 3.
notes.after: Move this paragraph so it opens the Social business model canvas section, before Key partners.

notes.anchor: are not the same person who benefits from the mission
notes.title: Payer and beneficiary split in one line
notes.body: This is the clearest business sentence on the page. It explains in one line why you need a social enterprise and why the canvas has two sides. Everything in section 3 follows from it.
notes.excerpt_note: Tec-Chihuahua splits one customer group by who actually pays, then names the buyer that creates.

notes.anchor: only 3.47% of Taiwan’s total farmland is organic and eco-friendly by 2024
notes.title: A number that changes your claim
notes.body: You give the figure, name the agency, add the global number, and then draw the consequence: without conventional farmers your market shrinks. That is the shape a judge trusts, because the number does work in the argument.
notes.excerpt_note: Each claim carries its source in the same sentence, with a comparison that sizes it for an outsider.

notes.anchor: Helped us better understand what it’s like for small farmers that face climate stress
notes.title: Name your first customer
notes.body: The ballot asks who would buy first. This section lists eight stakeholders but never says which one would place the first order, or what they said they would need before paying. Add a short block here called First potential customers.
notes.after: First potential customers. [Name], [role] at [organisation], told us they would trial [number] units if [condition]. We contacted them on [date].
notes.excerpt_note: Both winners name the company, say what it told them, and say who contacted whom.
notes.ballot: Has the team identified their first potential customers and their unmet need(s) that are not yet covered by existing solutions?

notes.anchor: Realized it’s not possible to compete price-wise with chemical fertilizers so we removed that from our business plan
notes.title: An expert changed your plan
notes.body: This is the most valuable sentence in the stakeholder section. An expert told you something, and you dropped a claim because of it. Keep writing changes this plainly.
notes.excerpt_note: Leiden says stakeholders talked it out of its own plan, then shows the new plan.
notes.ballot: Has the team outlined the skills, capabilities, and the stakeholders required to be credible in developing their solution further?

notes.anchor: Advised that we research more about regulations in Taiwan and any country we plan to expand to before actually taking action.
notes.title: Two entries are missing their change
notes.body: The CH Biotech and World Vegetable Centre entries stop at the advice. Four of your six entries have a “What we changed” line, which is what a judge is looking for. Add the missing two, even if the change was small or you decided not to act.
notes.after: What we changed. Started a country-by-country regulations table for Taiwan and each expansion market, which became section 7.
notes.ballot: Has the team outlined the skills, capabilities, and the stakeholders required to be credible in developing their solution further?

notes.anchor: Ms. Chen also emphasized the importance of addressing the concern that providing plants with external support
notes.title: You recorded a criticism of the product
notes.body: Ms. Chen's point cuts against your whole idea, and you wrote it down anyway and added it to your weaknesses. Judges read that as honesty, and it makes your positive claims easier to believe.
notes.excerpt_note: A GMO critic is quoted fairly and her concerns become testing obligations.
notes.ballot: Has the team considered the positive and negative long-term impacts of their fully developed solution?

notes.anchor: 399 million farms worldwide, or 70% of farmers report being affected by climate stress.
notes.title: Show the sum, fix farms and farmers
notes.body: This mixes farms and farmers in one line, and no source is given for either number. Write the multiplication so a judge can check one factor instead of doubting all three rings.
notes.after: Serviceable available market: 70% of farms report climate stress [source], so 570 million x 0.70 = 399 million farms.
notes.excerpt_note: Both winners print the multiplication and put a source on the contested factor.
notes.ballot: Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?

notes.anchor: there are around 4.7 million organic farms worldwide
notes.title: Your smallest market is the wrong farmers
notes.body: Here the obtainable market is organic farms. Two sections earlier you argue that over 97% of farmers are conventional, and in section 5.4 you write “Our target market is conventional smallholder farmers”. The Challenges box calls your demographic “smaller, sustainable farmers” again. Pick the group you sell to first and make all three places agree.
notes.ballot: Has the team identified their first potential customers and their unmet need(s) that are not yet covered by existing solutions?

notes.anchor: Our product is unlikely to be more effective than the current best chemical solutions
notes.title: You published a result against yourself
notes.body: Few teams write this sentence, and it buys trust for everything around it. It also tells a judge you know what you are competing on, which is speed and precision, not raw strength.
notes.excerpt_note: Both winners state the finding that goes against their own first proposal, then say what they do instead.

notes.anchor: which can price around 80,000 to 10,000NTD for just sensing or just protectant production
notes.title: This price range runs backwards
notes.body: The range goes from high to low, and NTD is stuck to the number. Also say which competitor each end of the range comes from.
notes.after: which cost about 10,000 to 80,000 NTD for sensing alone or protectant production alone ([company], [company])

notes.anchor: Our product is the first on the market that is able to respond in real time to the stresses faced by plants
notes.title: Add the limit to the first claim
notes.body: “First on the market” is the biggest claim on the page and nothing behind it checks the whole market. Put the limit of your knowledge in the same sentence, and name what you searched.
notes.after: From the [number] products we reviewed, and to the best of our knowledge, no existing system both senses plant stress and makes the protectant on site.
notes.excerpt_note: UToronto claims novelty and says in the same breath why it cannot be verified.
notes.ballot: Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?

notes.anchor: Eco-friendly, zero chemical residue
notes.title: Competitor table rows do not line up
notes.body: In the rendered table the feature names and the Yes/No answers have slipped out of order, so this feature appears where a company name should be, and only some columns get answers. A judge cannot tell which company has which feature. Rebuild it as one row per feature and one column per company, and give every No a source.
notes.ballot: Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?

notes.anchor: Our pricing strategy is designed around seasonal agricultural cash flow
notes.title: Price built around when farmers have money
notes.body: This opens the pricing section with a fact about your customer, not about your product. The base unit plus seasonal cartridge model then follows from it, which is exactly how a judge wants to read a pricing decision.
notes.excerpt_note: Padua measures the customer's routine first, then names the design decision that came out of it.
notes.ballot: Has the team identified their first potential customers and their unmet need(s) that are not yet covered by existing solutions?

notes.anchor: A possible solution would be a reusable drive and a replaceable cartridge system that aligns best with farmer spending behavior
notes.title: Last sentence repeats the second
notes.body: The paragraph already said the system is a low-cost reusable base unit with replaceable seasonal cartridges. This sentence says it again and calls it only a possibility, which weakens the earlier decision.
notes.after: Delete this sentence.

notes.anchor: First commercial pilot programs will launch in 2026
notes.title: 2026 here, 2027 in the timeline
notes.body: This objective puts the first pilots in 2026. The marketing timeline says “Our sales strategy will launch in 2027” under a chart titled 2027 Marketing Strategy, and the roadmap puts the Taiwan field pilot in Year 1.5 to 2.5. Fix the dates so the three agree, and state which year is Year 1.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: These locations have looser laws on GMOs and AgTech than areas such as Europe or Japan
notes.title: The EU cannot be looser than Europe
notes.body: The sentence before this one lists the European Union as a first, easier market, then this sentence contrasts those markets with Europe. The roadmap also puts the EU last, in Year 5.5 and later, and the Laws and Regulations page gives the order as Taiwan, European Union, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia. Three different orders exist across two pages. Agree one order and repeat it.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: uses a heavy-duty, single-button system with mechanically keyed cartridges to prove the device requires no digital skills
notes.title: One button here, a phone app earlier
notes.body: Section 2.2 says “The App brings everything together on the farmer’s phone”, with one-click ordering and an AIoT screen for setup. This paragraph says the device needs no digital skills and has one button. Both cannot be the product. If the app is optional, say so in section 2.2.

notes.anchor: Once these target farmers see a 10% to 15% increase in crop yields and a 20% to 30% drop in chemical spraying
notes.title: Say these are targets, not results
notes.body: A judge reading quickly will take these as measured results. Nothing on the page shows a field trial yet, so label them and say where they come from.
notes.after: Once our pilot farms reach our target of [number]% higher yield and [number]% less spraying, measured against their own previous season, we will launch a referral discount.
notes.excerpt_note: Aalto states what stage the project is at before it makes any claim, so the reader knows how to weigh the numbers.
notes.ballot: Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?

notes.anchor: By developing pilot programs through a 9-month period in total, we get to let farmers have a first hand experience
notes.title: Give the two trials, then the total
notes.body: The paragraph gives the total first, then the parts, then repeats itself in the last sentence. Reversing the order makes it shorter and clearer.
notes.after: We will run a 3-month trial in Q2, then use its feedback to design a 6-month trial across Q3 and Q4. Nine months of use tells us how farmers adapt to the system and what they would change.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: 1Concept validation Year 1 · 8/8 done
notes.title: Roadmap counts are in the text
notes.body: Your roadmap is readable as text, with eight of eight tasks marked done and a duration on every row. Many winning pages hid this in an image, where a judge reading the text cannot check it. This is one of the strongest answers on your page.
notes.excerpt_note: UToronto's status block is the same register: dated, countable, no adjectives.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: Validate shuttle vector, ccaSR system & MoClo 2.0
notes.title: Roadmap labels need a plain line
notes.body: The Year 1 rows are written for your lab, not for a business reader. Add one sentence under the chart that says what the year proves, in plain words.
notes.after: Year 1 proves the biology works in the lab: the light switch, the three protectants, and the bioreactor that holds the bacteria in.

notes.anchor: We target 20 to 30% fewer applications per season to directly lower labor and chemical waste
notes.title: A pilot target you can be judged on
notes.body: This is a number a farmer and a judge can both check at the end of a season, and it is tied to the two things your customer cares about, labour and chemicals. Keep targets written this way.
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: followed by the development of stress-tolerant (耐地氧) protectants
notes.title: Stray Chinese characters in the roadmap
notes.body: The bracketed characters do not translate the words before them and look like a leftover note. iGEM pages are read in English, so remove them or replace them with the term you meant.
notes.after: followed by the development of stress-tolerant protectants

notes.anchor: separating the physical hardware utility from the biological components into two bundles
notes.title: This sentence has no main verb
notes.body: The sentence starts with “Thus, to capture...” and never says who does what. Add the subject and the verb.
notes.after: We will therefore split the product into two bundles, one with the biology included and one without.

notes.anchor: Bundle B will be the standard bioreactor hardware sold standalone alongside a specialized software API
notes.title: Does containment still hold for Bundle B?
notes.body: Bundle B lets other labs grow their own strains in your hardware. Section 7 builds your whole regulatory case on your own contained strain. Say in one sentence who is responsible for biosafety in Bundle B, because a judge will ask.
notes.ballot: Has the team considered the positive and negative long-term impacts of their fully developed solution?

notes.anchor: Machine costs (in USD)
notes.title: Is this per unit or for 25 units?
notes.body: The row shows quantity 25 and $55,467, so a reader cannot tell whether a machine costs $55,467 or $2,219. The same question applies to the labour row. Add the unit to each row.
notes.after: Machine cost: 25 units at $[number] each = $55,467
notes.ballot: Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

notes.anchor: Break even point (units): total fixed cost / (selling price − total variable cost per unit)
notes.title: Fixed cost changes between table and sum

notes.title: The conclusion gives only good news
notes.body: The ballot asks for the negative long-term impacts of your finished product, and the page ends with positives only. You already have the material: the price barrier for small farms, cartridge and plastic waste, organic certification, and dependence on one supplier. Add two of them here, each with a cause and what you would do about it.
